correctness.rationale: For every nonzero real symmetric trace-zero 3-by-3 matrix, spectral normalization reduces the sign-area functional to H(u), u in [1/2,1], or 1-H(u). The uniform-sphere coordinate measure gives H(u)=E[g(1/2+(u-1/2)cos(2theta))]. The exact g derivatives prove strict concavity; paired derivative proves H strictly decreasing, with exact H(1/2)=1/sqrt(3) and H(1)=1/2. The zero set has measure zero, all equality cases follow from strictness, and -g>=5/(16sqrt(2)) yields the quantitative variance/Jensen rigidity coefficient. The packaged checker successfully verifies endpoint and curvature relations and independent representative integrations. These samples are not relied on for universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: The area of a sign region is a natural global nodal invariant of the full 5-dimensional real degree-two harmonic space, independent of topological nodal counts and not determined by even moments. Sharp universal positive-area extrema, complete axisymmetric equality classification, exactly balanced rank-two locus, monotone spectral interpolation, and quantitative stability solve a naturally complete classification rather than a hand-picked numerical slice. The explicit bound can guide sign-domain geometry and nodal asymmetry comparisons at low fixed degree.
